question: What happens to running Pods when a Deployment image is updated, and how does DeploymentStrategy control the transition?

ground_truth.answer: A Deployment uses the strategy field in DeploymentSpec to manage the transition. DeploymentStrategy has a type of RollingUpdate (default) or Recreate. With RollingUpdate, new Pods with the updated image are created incrementally while old Pods are terminated, keeping the application continuously available. The rollingUpdate field, a RollingUpdateDeployment, exposes maxUnavailable and maxSurge to control how many Pods can be unavailable or created above the desired count at any point. With Recreate, all existing Pods are terminated before new ones start, causing a brief downtime. progressDeadlineSeconds in DeploymentSpec bounds how long a rollout may stall before being declared failed.
context: io.k8s.api.apps.v1.DeploymentStrategy: type is RollingUpdate (default) or Recreate; rollingUpdate field is a RollingUpdateDeployment
io.k8s.api.apps.v1.RollingUpdateDeployment: maxUnavailable and maxSurge control rolling update pace and availability
io.k8s.api.apps.v1.DeploymentSpec: progressDeadlineSeconds sets the timeout before a stalled rollout is declared failed
